title: Micro contributor onboarding sprint journal
content:
Context / problem statement:

We keep losing momentum with early external contributors (community, partners) because the initial path to a meaningful PR is long: dev env setup, model access, private deployment gating, and opaque failure modes. Goal is a 1-day "first meaningful contribution" flow for engineers (not product users) so they can ship a small fix, integration, or sample app and feel the product velocity.

Constraints / principles:
- minimal infra/setup: local-first, then cloud step up
- reproducible: scripted, idempotent steps (no manual manual ssh fiddling)
- telemetry: capture where people get stuck (time spent per step)
- safe sandbox: avoid exposing production signings/keys, use ephemeral tokens for hosted API
- privacy/compliance: onboarding for private deployments must not leak customer artifacts

Target personas:
- external open-source contributors (familiar with Python/JS, little infra knowledge)
- solutions partners who want to add a quick connector to Redwood Dedicated
- internal new hires/contractors who need fast ramp

Success metrics (MVP):
- time-to-first-merge for a new contributor <= 8 hours (from having laptop to merged PR)
- self-serve completion rate >= 60% without SRE/DevEx help
- reduction in onboarding support tickets by 40% for new contributors in quarter after launch

MVP scope (what we build in Sprint):
1) a single canonical "hello-contributor" sample app (node + python) that calls Redwood API (hosted) with ephemeral tokens + unit test + CI that runs a smoke generation test
2) a scripted local dev environment using direnv / asdf / docker-compose that installs deps and runs tests (one-liner bootstrap)
3) an opt-in ephemeral hosted sandbox token generator (limited TTL + quota) for contributors to use instead of requiring org billing or dedicated capacity
4) quick docs page + a guided GitHub template (issue -> PR flow) and a CODE_OF_CONDUCT + CONTRIBUTING.md stub
5) telemetry hooks: short survey + step-completion pings (non-PII) to /dx-onboarding/track

User stories and acceptance criteria (rough):
- As a first-time contributor, I can run `./dev bootstrap` and have a reproducible local environment.
  - acceptance: script completes in <20 mins on mac/linux; outputs a `dev-ready` file; logs recorded

- As a contributor without billing, I can request an ephemeral sandbox token and make a test call to the hosted API.
  - acceptance: token TTL 24h, sandbox quota 1000 tokens/day, sample call returns 200 and a small 2-token response; token visible in dev config example

- As a maintainer, I can review a sample PR that includes a smoke test that runs on CI.
  - acceptance: PR template enforces smoke-test inclusion; CI job runs against simulator or sandbox (not prod)

- As a partner engineer doing Dedicated integration, I can run a local mock of the routing policy and verify fallback behavior.
  - acceptance: a `routing-mock` script that toggles model variant responses and a test harness that validates fallback policy triggers

Open questions / risk log:
- Token service: will security team allow a public/ephemeral token endpoint? (TBD with security, risk low if rate-limited)
- Hosted sandbox cost — needs quota protections. How to bill external partner usage? (use credits pool + alerting)
- Private deployment onboarding: how much can we automate without customer infra access? likely need a separate trimmed checklist + SRE consult.
- Windows support: lower priority, but should not block MVP if Linux/mac covered.

MVP technical notes / implementation sketch:
- Bootstrap script (POSIX): checks asdf/node/pyenv, sets up virtualenv, creates .env from `.env.template`, installs dev CLI `redwoodctl` locally via `pipx` or `npm link` sample
- Sandbox token generator: small Django/Express endpoint behind auth (GitHub OAuth + limited grant flow) that mints scoped tokens via internal service account. Simple UI: one-click request + README explains TTL
- Sample app: `examples/hello-contributor` with two folders: `node/` and `python/` each with README showing sample streaming call, predictions, and sample unit test that asserts 200 + response contains safe sentinel text
- CI job: `ci/onboarding-smoke.yml` that: checks out PR, runs `./dev bootstrap` in container, obtains sandbox token from secrets manager (only on main/test branches), runs smoke tests

Observability / telemetry:
- tiny analytics collector: step pings (bootstrap-start, bootstrap-finish, token-request, smoke-test-pass/fail) -> internal bucket in DX project
- collect logs of common failures (missing asdf, pyenv, docker not running) and map to help-snippets in docs

Docs skeleton (one-pager):
- TL;DR: 1-liner + video gif showing "clone -> bootstrap -> run test -> open PR" (30s)
- Pre-reqs: mac/linux, git, Docker optional
- Step-by-step: clone repo, run `./dev bootstrap`, run tests `./dev test`, open PR from feature branch
- Ephemeral tokens: request flow and limits
- Troubleshooting: common fixes + links to Slack channel #dx-onboard

Rollout plan (2 sprints):
Sprint 1 (MVP): build scripts, sample app, docs, sandbox token endpoint, CI smoke job, telemetry. Internal alpha with 10 volunteers.
Sprint 2: polish UX, add Windows support, add Dedicated onboarding mock, instrument improved telemetry, public beta for community onboarding.

Experiment ideas / follow-ups:
- "Onboarding buddy" microtask: pair first-time contributors with a maintainer for 30 minutes via a booking link (measure impact on merge time)
- Automated contributor grading: small badge if contributor's PR passes smoke tests + linter without maintainer edits -> incentivize repeat contributions
- Starter-labeler bot: if PR created with `onboard` label, bot auto-checks bootstrap script and posts inline checklist to PR

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to Security about ephemeral token design and rate limits (runbook for misuse) — owner: Rowan (this week)
- Draft CONTRIBUTING.md and PR template (Tess to own)
- Wire a quick GH Action to run smoke tests against sandbox (Devon to prototype)
- Recruit 10 internal volunteers across DX/serving-runtime/solutions for alpha test (Mira to coordinate)

Rough timeline:
- Sep 22: initial bootstrap script committed, docs stub up
- Sep 30: sandbox token endpoint prototype + CI smoke job
- Oct 06: internal alpha with 10 contributors, capture telemetry
- Oct 14: iterate on pain points and publish public beta checklist

Snippets (copy/paste to README):
- One-liner to bootstrap (POSIX):
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redwood-inference/onboard/main/bootstrap.sh | bash

- Minimal test (python):
  python -c "from redwood import Client; c=Client(token="$REDWOOD_TOKEN"); r=c.generate("hello"); assert 'hello' in r.text.lower()"

Closing thought: make it feel magical — the surprising delight of getting an immediate green CI + a maintainers thumbs-up will convert casual tinkerers into repeat contributors. Keep the surface area small and instrument everything.

-- Rowan J. Blake
(Drafts: iterating; not final)
